purpose: EXPERIMENT B - single-class generic litter localiser. Offline only.
transform: class id -> 0 ('litter'). Boxes, images and split membership are untouched.

leakage.split_strategy: Inherited verbatim from datasets/taco_yolo, which splits by TACO image id. No re-split was performed here, so Experiment A and Experiment B evaluate on byte-identical test images.

TUD-GV.reason: Water-surface domain, fixed camera, all 1920x1080. 95.94% of boxes cover under 1% of the frame and the LARGEST is 4.98%. TACO's largest is 94%. The production failure is an indoor hand-held close-up, which this distribution contains zero examples of; adding it would pull the model further from the failing case.

IWHR.reason: Water-surface 'floater', 1920x1080. Same domain objection as TUD-GV. 'floater' is also a different annotation concept from 'litter on the ground'.

Flow-Img.reason: Train split only - no val, no test, so it cannot be held out and would leak into any evaluation built from it. 93.87% of boxes under 1% of frame. Class is 'bottle', an object claim, and the export could not be verified against an archive (FLOW_DATASET_AUDIT.md section 0).

garbage_Dataset.reason: Classification only. Zero bounding boxes. Used for the material classifier, never for detection.

excluded_sources._note: Excluded, not discarded. Each is a candidate for a later arm that tests domain transfer explicitly. Merging them into arm B would confound the one variable this experiment isolates: the class dimension.

known_limitation_negative_images: NO source contains a single image without litter - TACO 0, TUD-GV 0, IWHR 0, Flow-Img 0 background images. A detector trained on any of them has never been shown a frame whose correct answer is 'nothing here'. This is measured, not assumed, and it is the structural reason a litter localiser is expected to fire on people and furniture.
